_about: The commentator's preparation sheet: background that is true before kick-off. Input to the colour voice, like the lineups. 'about' is a player's name as it appears in the lineup, a team name, or 'match'. Facts as of the day of the final, 18 December 2022.

notes.text: This is the World Cup final at the Lusail Stadium, in front of almost 89,000 people.
Szymon Marciniak of Poland is the referee tonight.
Messi and Mbappé are club-mates at Paris Saint-Germain, and came into this final level on five goals each in the race for the Golden Boot.
Argentina are chasing a third World Cup, and their first since 1986.
Argentina lost their opening game of this tournament to Saudi Arabia, in this very stadium.
Argentina lost the final in 2014 to Germany; several of this squad still carry that.
Argentina came through a penalty shoot-out against the Netherlands in the quarter-final after letting a two-goal lead slip.
Argentina are the champions of South America; they won the Copa América last year.
Lionel Scaloni has been in charge of Argentina since 2018, a first senior job as a head coach.
France are the holders. No team has retained the World Cup since Brazil in 1962.
Didier Deschamps won this trophy as a player in 1998 and as a coach in 2018.
France came here without Benzema, Pogba and Kanté, all injured.
There was illness in the French camp in the days before this final.
France beat England in the quarter-final and Morocco in the semi-final to get here.
Messi is 35, and has said this will be the last World Cup match of a remarkable career.
This is Messi's 26th World Cup match, more than any player in history.
This is Messi's fifth World Cup, and the one trophy still missing.
Mbappé scored in the 2018 final as a teenager, and turns 24 on Tuesday.
Mbappé already has a World Cup winner's medal, at 23.
Di María is back in the starting eleven for the final after an injury earlier in the tournament.
Di María scored the winning goal in last year's Copa América final against Brazil.
Álvarez is 22 and came into the final with four goals in this tournament.
Álvarez only became a starter during this tournament, and plays club football at Manchester City.
Fernández is 21, plays for Benfica, and started this tournament on the bench.
Mac Allister plays for Brighton in the Premier League; this has been a breakthrough tournament.
De Paul is the engine of this Argentina midfield, an Atlético Madrid player.
Martínez, the Aston Villa goalkeeper, was the hero of the shoot-out against the Netherlands.
Otamendi is 34, the senior man in that Argentina defence.
Romero plays for Tottenham, where Hugo Lloris is club captain.
Molina plays for Atlético Madrid, alongside De Paul and France's Griezmann.
Lloris is France's captain and their most-capped player of all time.
Giroud is 36 and became France's all-time leading scorer during this tournament.
Griezmann has played a deeper midfield role in this tournament and has been one of France's best players.
Dembélé plays for Barcelona and was part of the squad that won it in 2018.
Rabiot plays for Juventus, as Di María does.
Tchouaméni is 22, plays for Real Madrid, and scored against England in the quarter-final.
Varane started the 2018 final as well, and knows what it takes to win one of these.
Theo Hernández scored France's first goal in the semi-final against Morocco.
Kolo Muani scored within a minute of coming on in the semi-final.
Marcus Thuram is the son of Lilian Thuram, who won the World Cup with France in 1998.
Coman plays for Bayern Munich and once scored the winning goal in a Champions League final.
Camavinga is just 20 and plays for Real Madrid.
Koundé is a centre-back by trade, playing at right-back for France in this tournament.
Upamecano plays for Bayern Munich.
These two met in the last sixteen four years ago, and France won that one 4-3.
Argentina and France have each won this trophy twice before tonight.
This is the first World Cup played in November and December.
Argentina beat Croatia 3-0 in the semi-final, with Álvarez scoring twice.
Argentina came into this tournament on a 36-match unbeaten run.
France were champions in 1998 and 2018, and beaten finalists in 2006.
Mbappé and Giroud scored nine of France's goals between them on the way to this final.
Messi has scored in every knockout round of this tournament.
Messi was named the best player of the 2014 World Cup, and lost the final.
Di María also scored the winning goal in the Olympic final back in 2008.
Di María missed the 2014 final through injury.
Mbappé was only the second teenager to score in a World Cup final, after Pelé.
Griezmann scored in the 2018 final and was named man of the match that day.
Giroud plays for AC Milan, and went through the whole of the 2018 World Cup without scoring.
Lloris is captaining France in a second successive World Cup final.
Varane plays for Manchester United, and won the Champions League four times with Real Madrid.
Theo Hernández came into the side when Lucas Hernández, the older brother, was injured in the opening game.
Upamecano missed the semi-final through illness.
Rabiot missed the semi-final through illness, and is straight back in tonight.
Martínez only made an Argentina debut last year, at the age of 28.
Otamendi plays for Benfica, as Enzo Fernández does.
Tagliafico plays club football in France, with Lyon.
Mac Allister's father played for Argentina too, alongside Diego Maradona.
Fernández scored against Mexico in the group stage, a first goal for Argentina.
Molina scored in the quarter-final against the Netherlands, from a Messi pass.
Lautaro Martínez scored the winning penalty in the shoot-out against the Netherlands.
Montiel plays for Sevilla, as Acuña does.
Acuña plays for Sevilla in Spain.
Paredes is at Juventus, on loan from Paris Saint-Germain.
Dybala plays for Roma, and has hardly featured in this tournament.
Pezzella plays for Real Betis.
Konaté plays for Liverpool, and started the semi-final.
Fofana plays for Monaco, and started the semi-final in midfield.
Disasi plays for Monaco.
Whoever wins tonight gets a third star on the shirt.
This is the third World Cup meeting of these two; Argentina won in 1930 and 1978, France in 2018.
Marciniak is the first Polish referee to take charge of a World Cup final.
It is the eighteenth of December, Qatar's national day.
This is Argentina's sixth World Cup final.
Argentina beat Mexico and Poland to get out of the group after that opening defeat.
Argentina beat Australia 2-1 in the last sixteen.
The Argentina support in this stadium is enormous; it has felt like a home game all tournament.
Scaloni is 44, the youngest coach at this World Cup, and played for Argentina at the 2006 tournament.
Scaloni has put Di María on the left tonight, a change from where Di María usually plays.
This is France's fourth World Cup final, and a second in a row.
France are the first team to reach back-to-back finals since Brazil in 2002.
Deschamps has been in charge of France for ten years.
France lost to Tunisia in the group stage, with a much-changed team.
France are without Benzema, the holder of the Ballon d'Or, injured on the eve of the tournament.
Messi came into this final with five goals and three assists in the tournament.
Messi is Argentina's record scorer and record appearance-maker, and has won the Ballon d'Or seven times.
Messi had a penalty saved against Poland in the group stage, and has scored the others since.
Mbappé had nine World Cup goals before tonight, at the age of 23.
Mbappé scored twice against Denmark and twice against Poland on the way here.
Di María is 34, and has said this will be a last World Cup.
Di María joined Juventus from Paris Saint-Germain in the summer.
Álvarez joined Manchester City from River Plate this year.
Álvarez scored twice in the semi-final against Croatia.
Fernández only joined Benfica from River Plate in the summer.
Mac Allister scored against Poland in the group stage, a first goal for Argentina.
De Paul spent five years at Udinese before the move to Atlético Madrid.
Martínez saved two penalties in the quarter-final shoot-out against the Netherlands.
Martínez spent the best part of ten years at Arsenal, most of it out on loan.
Romero is 24, and joined Tottenham from Atalanta.
Molina moved to Atlético Madrid from Udinese in the summer.
Tagliafico spent four years at Ajax before the move to Lyon.
Acuña missed the semi-final through suspension.
Montiel missed the semi-final through suspension.
Lautaro Martínez started this tournament as first choice, and lost the place to Álvarez.
Lloris broke the French appearance record in the quarter-final against England.
Griezmann set up both French goals in the quarter-final against England.
Griezmann is France's leading provider of assists of all time.
Giroud scored the winner against England in the quarter-final, with a header.
Dembélé is 25, and has started every knockout game on the right.
Rabiot scored France's first goal of this tournament, against Australia.
Tchouaméni joined Real Madrid from Monaco in the summer.
Koundé joined Barcelona from Sevilla in the summer.
Theo Hernández plays club football for AC Milan, alongside Giroud.
Kolo Muani plays for Eintracht Frankfurt, and was a late call-up to this squad.
Marcus Thuram plays for Borussia Mönchengladbach.
Camavinga has been used at left-back in this tournament, though midfield is the natural position.
